abstract_summary: Persistent memory has enabled large language model (LLM) agents to store factual knowledge, prior decisions, reasoning histories, tool usage information, and context. While this has improved the agent's functionality and continuity across tasks, it has also introduced a new attack surface: the agent's own reasoning...
citation: Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own: Forged Reasoning Attacks on LLM Agent Memory and Defenses. Neeraj Karamchandani, Piyush Nagasubramaniam, Sencun Zhu, Dinghao Wu. 2026-07-06. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05029

LLM agent's reasoning store as a distinct
attack surface and introduce FARMA, a novel two-
phase memory poisoning attack that forges an agent's
own decision logs using evasive language and self-
amplification.
2) We propose SENTINEL, a 5-layer defense pipeline
whose reasoning guard, to the best of our knowledge,
is the first defense work that structurally analyzes rea-
soning traces to detect forged entries.
3) We conduct a comprehensive evaluation across three
agent domains and three models. We show that FARMA
defeats existing defenses while SENTINEL drops attack
success rate to as low as 0% with zero false positives
across 326 benign traces.
4) We show that our Reasoning Guard is the primary
load-bearing component against FARMA, while the
lightweight outer layers contribute defense in depth
against orthogonal attack variants.

main contributions. We use heuristic checks (string matching,
regex, simple scoring) rather than an LLM-based judge for
cost and latency reasons: per-write overhead is under 1 ms,
which lets SENTINEL run as a synchronous filter on the
memory-write path without a second LLM call or interference
with the agent's system prompt. We also considered using
a supervised classifier instead of a heuristic approach for
Reasoning Guard, but since we are targeting a new attack
surface, the representative labeled training data would not be
available. Such ML classifiers can be complementary to our
work and are left for future work.

regex, simple scoring) rather than an LLM-based judge for
cost and latency reasons: per-write overhead is under 1 ms,
which lets SENTINEL run as a synchronous filter on the
memory-write path without a second LLM call or interference
with the agent's system prompt. We also considered using
a supervised classifier instead of a heuristic approach for
Reasoning Guard, but since we are targeting a new attack
surface, the representative labeled training data would not be
available. Such ML classifiers can be complementary to our
work and are left for future work.

B. Measurements
We measure attack success against a clean-memory base-
line, consistent with the differential-evaluation protocol used
in prior memory-poisoning work [7]. For each (task, defense)
cell, we run the agent twice: once with an empty memory
store and no attack injection (the clean baseline), and once
after FARMA has injected forged content (the poisoned run).
Both runs use the same task and identical seeds. An attack is
counted as successful if and only if the clean baseline pro-
duced a safe-careful action AND the poisoned run produced
the attacker-target action. This differential definition isolates
attack-caused behavior change from the agent's natural default
action on a task.

that agents in binary-decision domains (clinical-data imports,

We evaluate FARMA against A-MemGuard's heuristic con-
figuration as well as LLM-as-a-judge configuration. FARMA
bypasses both of them. Intuitively, A-MemGuard's defense
that should catch the anomalous behavior of FARMA's entries,
but does not due to FARMA's use of amplification cycles.
The amplification cycle basically floods the memory store with
consistent forged traces, so the outlier signal is no longer an
outlier. SENTINEL is the only defense that reduces FARMA's
attack success rate to as low as 0% across domains. These
results motivate the need for structural analysis of reasoning-
trace content rather than statistical or lexical approaches alone.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported ASR reductions and zero false positives are established through task-level differential execution and clean-trace filtering rather than through the Reasoning Guard's own scoring [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0043, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are measured by differential end-to-end task execution, comparing safe baseline actions against poisoned-run actions, plus false-positive filtering on 326 benign traces [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0043, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The Reasoning Guard's heuristic signals and pattern matchers are derived from FARMA templates and system-security concepts, with thresholds and weights tuned to the attack corpus [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0030, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0036].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that FARMA bypasses keyword and consensus defenses (e.g., A-MemGuard) and achieves high attack success are well substantiated by the differential evaluation tables [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0048, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0049]. Claims regarding SENTINEL's mitigation to 0% ASR on EHR and zero false positives align with documented experimental results [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0049, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The authors evaluate FARMA and SENTINEL across three agent domains (EHR, ReAct-QA, RAP) and three LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Llama 3.3 70B) over 50 trials using rigorous differential baselines and Wilson 95% confidence intervals [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0043, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0049]. Layer ablations isolate the Reasoning Guard's contribution, and false positive rates are tested on 326 benign traces [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0046, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is evaluated based on differential end-to-end task execution decisions and false-positive checks on 326 independent clean traces [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0043, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Task-level differential execution outcome (whether the agent executed the unsafe skipped-validation action versus safe baseline action) and false-positive filtering on benign traces [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0043, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Predefined heuristic rules and pattern matchers derived from FARMA templates and system-security concepts [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0026, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0030, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0036].

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report that the heuristic Reasoning Guard is susceptible to an adaptive paraphrase attacker with knowledge of the detection patterns [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0051]. They also note limitations regarding simulated single-agent environments rather than live production multi-agent systems [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0051, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0052].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology clearly formalizes the threat and system models along with the 5-layer defense pipeline [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0017, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0026, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0030]. The central Reasoning Guard integrates five concrete heuristic structural forgery signals into a composite admission score that executes synchronously with low overhead [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0030, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0034, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0038].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a scoped and novel security insight into LLM agent memory vulnerability, provides an explicit threat model and defense design, and validates claims through controlled empirical baselines and ablations across multiple domains and models.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper identifies persistent reasoning memory in LLM agents as an attack vector and introduces FARMA, a two-phase attack that injects and amplifies forged rationale traces [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0006, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0007, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0010]. It also proposes SENTINEL, a 5-layer filtering pipeline centering on a structural Reasoning Guard to detect forged decision records [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0009, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0010, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0026].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a scoped and novel security insight into LLM agent memory vulnerability, provides an explicit threat model and defense design, and validates claims through controlled empirical baselines and ablations across multiple domains and models.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report that the heuristic Reasoning Guard is susceptible to an adaptive paraphrase attacker with knowledge of the detection patterns [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0051]. They also note limitations regarding simulated single-agent environments rather than live production multi-agent systems [E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0051, E546cf0cdb8ace3c7-B0052].
